title: Extraction of Meiofauna and Meioflora from Aquatic Environmental Samples
author: Daisuke Shimada

steps.title: Collect environmental substrates
steps.instruction: Gather sediments, seagrasses, seaweeds, sessile animals, or other substrates by hand or using appropriate sampling devices.

steps.title: Wash substrate in bucket
steps.instruction: Transfer 100–500 ml of substrate into a bucket and wash with ~10 × that volume of tap water (or 3.5 % MgCl₂ for fragile animals such as turbellarians). Stir gently, wait ≥10 min, then stir gently again. If the substrate is mud, limit the volume to ≤50 ml.

steps.title: Transport substrates to laboratory
steps.instruction: Move the whole substrate to the laboratory at low temperature, or if that is impractical, freeze the material or store it in DESS solution (accepting possible injury to organisms).

steps.title: Filter supernatant through nylon mesh
steps.instruction: Immediately pass the supernatant through a 10–100 μm nylon mesh (commonly 32 μm or 63 μm). Smaller meshes collect more organisms but clog more easily. Repeat this filtration step once or twice.

steps.title: Remove and wash nylon mesh
steps.instruction: Carefully lift the nylon mesh from the bottle, turn it over, and wash it in a Petri dish with 20 ml filtered seawater. For large substrate amounts or a clogged mesh, transfer the material to a Petri dish with a dropper after each filtration.

steps.title: Transfer filtrate to sampling bottle
steps.instruction: Move the entire seawater containing the collected material into a 25–50 ml sampling bottle; split into several bottles if necessary.

steps.title: Heat bottle to kill organisms
steps.instruction: Place the sampling bottle in water at 80–90 °C for 2 min to kill organisms and inactivate DNase. (If targeting very small, live organisms such as tardigrades, the order of heating, fixation, and sorting may be altered.)

steps.title: Add DESS preservation solution
steps.instruction: Add 5–10 × the volume of DESS solution to the material, mix thoroughly, and store; the sample remains viable for >10 years.

steps.title: Prepare DESS solution (1 L)
steps.instruction: 1) Dissolve 93.0 g Na₂‑EDTA in 400 ml deionized water while stirring and gradually adding NaOH; adjust pH to 7.5–8.0 and add water to a total volume of 500 ml (0.5 M EDTA). 2) Mix this 0.5 M EDTA solution with 200 ml (or 200 g) DMSO, then add deionized water to reach 1 000 ml. 3) Add a saturated amount of NaCl and stir well (precipitation is acceptable).

steps.title: Construct Irwin loop
steps.instruction: Cut stainless‑steel wire (0.2–0.3 mm diameter) into 10 cm and 5 cm pieces; attach the longer piece to a suitable handle with water‑resistant adhesive, bend the loop to a convenient angle with pliers, and rinse the loop with deionized water after each use.

steps.title: Construct nylon‑mesh filter apparatus
steps.instruction: Remove the bottom of a 500‑ or 1 000‑ml wide‑mouth screw‑cap plastic bottle, cut a piece of nylon mesh larger than the bottle mouth, place the mesh over the mouth, fasten tightly with rubber bands, hook the pieces together and twist with pliers leaving small loops, then fix the longer piece to a handle with adhesive.

steps.title: Settle organisms and remove supernatant
steps.instruction: Allow the filtered material to stand for 10 min so organisms settle at the bottom, then remove as much supernatant as possible with a dropper.

steps.title: Pick organisms and store in DESS tubes
steps.instruction: Transfer the settled sample to a Petri dish, pick individual organisms under a stereomicroscope using the Irwin loop, and place each into a 2.0‑ml screw‑cap micro‑tube containing DESS solution; rinse the loop with deionized water after each pick.
